t.E162.agn: In 2015 EFSA stated that the toxicological data were not sufficient to set an ADI; however, it explained that betanin intake from the additive is in the same range as that from a normal diet and that there is no safety concern at the reported use levels. In 1987 JECFA set the ADI as 'not specified'.
t.E162.body: Betanin is poorly absorbed when taken orally; in rats most of it was broken down in the digestive tract, with about 3% of the dose excreted in urine and a similar amount in faeces.
t.E162.found.0: In the EU, as a Group II colour in many foods at quantum satis: flavoured fermented milk products and cheeses, confectionery and chewing gum, breakfast cereals, fine bakery wares, sauces, mustard and seasonings, flavoured drinks, cider and fruit wines, snacks
t.E162.found.1: Canned red fruit and canned vegetables
t.E162.found.4: Fish and crustacean pastes, cooked crustaceans
t.E162.prod: Obtained by pressing red beetroot or by water extraction.
t.E162.regx.0: Re-evaluated; data insufficient for an ADI, no safety concern at reported uses.
t.E162.regx.2: Group II colour: quantum satis in the authorised food categories.
t.E162.summary: A red-purple colour obtained from red beetroot. Used in yoghurt, ice cream, confectionery and drinks.
t.E162.what: A red-purple colour obtained from red beetroot, containing mainly betanin.
